title: Add athena land --pr for owned mode with a REST-only gh client
summary: Build the command slice D86 deferred: `athena land --pr <job>` pushes the job's branch through `check_push`, opens a PR, waits for green checks, and then lands only when it observes the merge, with `check_merged` as the final check. The host client shells out to `gh api` REST paths only. Per the user's reply, Athena merges via REST only when a setting, off by default, opts in; otherwise it stops at an open, green PR.

defaults_applied.how: All new code is Rust; the gh CLI is only an external program invoked, no scripts.
Shell out to the maintained gh CLI rather than adding an HTTP crate; the call is recorded in a decision.
Fake runner/host tests cover each outcome; cargo test and clippy are clean.
One slice: the owned-mode command only, not stealth mode or auto-merge.
A test asserts every recorded gh api call is REST and never graphql; merge only runs when the setting is on.
Docs and the decision entry are written for an outside reader.

assumptions: The opt-in is a boolean setting in athena.toml's config struct (athena-data config), default false, named something like land.merge; its name is the producer's call and is documented.

Without opt-in, the command opens the PR, waits for checks, reports 'open, green; merge it yourself', and exits; a later `athena land --pr <job>` run (or the same command re-run) looks up the stored link, observes the merge via REST, and runs check_merged.

The REST calls are: GET git ref and compare for the remote head, POST pulls, GET commits/{sha}/check-runs and status, PUT pulls/{n}/merge (opt-in only), and GET pulls/{n} for merged state and merge_commit_sha.
The push itself uses git (not gh), after check_push; the branch is the job's work branch, with no force.
Check waiting uses an injected clock/poll interval and a timeout, so tests do not sleep.
Athena's own governance files (athena.toml) do not change; the new setting lives in code defaults.

acceptance_criteria.text: A new host-client module in crates/athena-core implements `Host` and new traits (open PR, read check status, merge) by running `gh api` with REST paths only. No source contains `graphql` outside the test that asserts its absence, and no `gh pr` subcommand is used.
The CLI has `athena land --pr <job>` with an optional `--json`, wired in crates/athena-cli and documented in `--help`.

The push goes through `check_push` first and has no force option. The link is saved with `store_link`, outcomes go through `apply_outcome`, and the link survives `clean_job` until the merge is observed.

A setting, default off, decides whether Athena merges. When off, Athena never calls the merge endpoint; it stops at an open PR with green checks and reports that. When on, it merges via the REST merge endpoint.
Landing is recorded only after the merge is observed by PR number and `check_merged` returns Verified; a merge of other content gives merged-unverified.

Run `cargo test`. Fake-runner tests pass for: green checks with merge off (no merge call, PR left open), merge on (merged then landed), failed checks (no merge), check timeout, non-fast-forward push refused, merged-unverified, and every recorded gh api call is REST (no graphql).
Run `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check`; both are clean. `cargo test` for the whole workspace passes, including the existing pr.rs tests.

docs/decisions.md has a new entry recording the buy-first call (gh versus an HTTP crate), the REST-only choice, and the merge opt-in. docs/design/native-pr-landing.md says the command is built, and CHANGELOG.md has an entry.

out_of_scope: Force pushes or pushing branches other than the job's work branch
Changes to athena.toml, CI workflows, or other governance files
departures: Larger than the reference: a new client module, CLI wiring, a config setting, many fake-based tests, and three docs, so cost and time are higher and verification is less likely to pass.
